# W1 native projection contract architecture — proposal r1

Status: **design proposal for fresh independent architecture review; no implementation or admission**. Local Codex/macOS, 2026-10-05. Root is sole lander. P1/P2/P3 are accepted inputs, not reconciled again here. No repository or author worktree was modified.

## Journey and recommendation

J1: I select my already accepted `Affiliation.ror_id` field and discover organization context from admitted metadata. Good result: explanation identifies the exact user contract, raw field, native sources and checked projection; no data lookup. J2: I inspect the organization → ordered locations → place graph, its independent country/admin1 branches and optional aliases. Good result: scope, attribution, multiplicity and bounds are visible. J3: I explicitly run it. Good result: bounded ordinary reads produce distinct affiliation, location and alias grains. J4: I inspect matched, invalid, unmatched, ambiguous and incomplete outcomes without losing parents. J5: I save, reopen, check changed metadata and explicitly continue or rerun. Good result: every graph/stage/operator/source/runtime pin is retained; changed pins require review; reopening is idle. J6: I decline, wait or cancel. Good result: no implicit request, and cancellation terminates active work.

Recommend a **separate, closed native graph member** in an additive `ovdb-representation-contract/4` attachment envelope. Keep the existing `representation_contract: {path, sha256}` publisher/Directory link. The new envelope has one optional local `legacy` reference to the existing unchanged format 1/2/3 document and exactly one graph. This is a one-level composition, never a recursive import system. The graph executes only this accepted source-qualified W1 topology. Keep the existing ROR user contract and every legacy contract byte unchanged; do not widen native-identifier or replace its decision pin. Publish the accepted new decision in the existing DataTug evidence area and reference it from the graph's existing-shaped `decision` field, but never treat its prose as executable authority.

Use related result sets inside the existing DataTug query/service/Worker path: affiliations, location context, alias children. Reuse DALgo exact joins over bounded local caches; projection produces app-owned derived rows alongside native data. Do not add a generic expression language, server relational execution, new dataset registry or fresh Geo selection.

## Exact evidence and why existing mechanisms are insufficient

All repository claims here refer to exact Git objects, **not fresh remote-head claims**. The supplied app candidate is frozen r1 patch, not the author's repairing worktree. `source-evidence.json` records exact extracted bytes/hashes. Inspected:

- OVDB publisher `27f2664782e01feb4fb5938f28b8f8eae0a868a8`, released baseline supplied by root; `publisher/representation/{schema.json,schema2.json,schema3.json,contract.go,native.go,attachment.go,strict.go}`.
- App `413bb772e04f139210adec92ad0cb3fce2b07883`; frozen `artifact:data-fabric-w1-app-bounded-runtime/candidate-r1.patch`. Candidate known budget findings are not accepted or repeated as solved here.
- DALgo JS `1534acd4d0e4a104c58eba09fb9c25619efc8f24`, package version 0.2.0; app package.json selects that exact revision.
- Directory companion cached object `d946bd032b31d590fce0ebafc56537c0b77dcfad`, `scripts/lib/representation.mjs`; no current-remote assertion.
- ROR `dc78c1e929f1f10018f8c39e690351059a50c71f`, native SQLite `afdf9781…d5d38`, model `9694a0b6…ae`; Geo `6f4cf1269bc393048f6b204069135a62f0bb6c02`, native SQLite `cb53af14…456d`, model `609fe73e…81`. Exact full values in example/evidence. No newer Geo candidate is selected.

| Existing surface | Actual checked behavior | Consequence |
|---|---|---|
| Format 1 | closed label bridge; string single-property source; identity transform; zero-or-one | cannot represent native integer P1, two-component P2, or reverse enumeration |
| Format 2 | closed discriminated label-bridge/native-identifier; native equal namespaces, string source/target; required single-property target key | native location composite identity and integer-to-string projection cannot be passed as native identity |
| Format 3 | native only, adds exact external source.data; all identity restrictions remain | source.data provides artifact identity, not new operations |
| `Check`, `checkNative`, `checkSnapshot` | external source schema, provider-local target/native files, duplicate single source refusal, single target key and native receipt association | blanket loosening would silently change old contract semantics |
| `ParseAttachment` and Directory envelope | exactly local JSON path and SHA256 | natural extension point; no manifest field is needed |
| `decision.document` | immutable external file bytes verified; app explicitly says provenance, not a free-prose acceptance parser | cannot hide an operator/approval in prose |
| App `SourceField`, `PublicDataScenario` | datatype string; saved projection identity; one attachment/model/decision | need additive graph-specific saved pins, not fabricated string model |
| `BoundedSource`, `validateBounds` | one parent field, two-to-four stages; candidate loads string filter values | cannot produce P1/P2; seven-stage branch cannot be claimed as a linear plan |
| DALgo DTQL | equality join fields and arithmetic expression variants; no arbitrary conversion/composite callback in query model | a SQL/DTQL cast or ad-hoc callback in saved text neither carries authority nor validates source pins |
| Saved query/runtime pins | persist query/projection/bounds and four runtime pins | useful storage, insufficient authority until graph attachment is checked/admitted |

Rejected alternatives: changing native source datatypes; accepting all numbers in current string path; putting transformation rules in decision prose; a generated string column in the canonical source model; a new global transform registry. A graph only inside user-editable `federation` would be an unadmitted authority. A separate manifest graph field would duplicate the existing attachment machinery. An additive format is required because old schema `additionalProperties:false` and transform/cardinality constants must keep rejecting these changes.

## Minimal serialized extension

`contract-example-r1.json` is the concrete serialized design template. It includes exact selected native refs and every physical edge. Values beginning `UNPUBLISHED_` deliberately fail validation: the accepted scratch decision has no committed immutable decision pin yet, and the final admitted ROR/Geo attachment revisions are not known. Do not invent those hashes or use the app fixture as canonical publication. The outer Geo publisher will point its existing attachment field to a new file, e.g. `representation-graph.json`. `legacy` points at the unchanged previous Geo attachment JSON at that same outer provider revision. ROR's attachment stays unchanged and is referenced as the graph entry.

Envelope keys are exactly `format`, optional `legacy`, and `graphs`. `legacy` is a single local path/SHA reference, never self-reference; its document must be format 1, 2 or 3 and passes the existing checker with its original format and outer provider context. No format 4 nested dependency is allowed. The graph entry attachment is likewise limited to one exact format 2/3 document and one `contractIndex`, checked against full selected source and target identity; no recursive graph resolution. In particular, the new document is **not** a mixed array that retrospectively reinterprets older contracts under format 4.

Graph keys and enums are closed, as in the example. `execution=native-graph`, `id=w1-ror-geonames-context/1`, `resultShape=affiliations-location-context-aliases/1` are finite checked capabilities. `sources` has exactly `ror` and `geo`; `stages` has exactly six public stages plus the existing entry's user stage; `edges` has exactly the five additional edges below (six total with entry). Aliases is the sole optional requested branch. Unknown members, IDs, topology, operators, additional fields/edges, cycles, backward edges or duplicate IDs fail before any data request. This finite implementation is not a generic graph interpreter.

| From → to | Raw fields → lookup field | Projection | Cardinality/grain |
|---|---|---|---|
| Existing user → organizations | `Affiliation.ror_id` → `id` | original admitted ROR contract | zero-or-one; affiliation parent |
| organizations → locations | `id` → `organization_id` | `exact-string/1` | zero-or-many; `(organization_id,ordinal)` |
| locations → places | `geonames_id:int` → `geonameid:string` | `ror-positive-int-geonames-decimal/1` | zero-or-one |
| places → countries | `country_code` → `iso` | `exact-string/1` | zero-or-one |
| places → admin1 | ordered `(country_code,admin1_code)` → `code` | `geonames-country-admin1/1` | zero-or-one |
| places → aliases | `geonameid` → `geonameid` | `exact-string/1` | zero-or-many; `alternate_name_id` |

Dispatch is a closed switch over `(graph capability, edge ID, ordered source fields/types, source model/dataset hashes, target fields/types/model/dataset hashes, operator version)`, derived from the checked graph. IDs alone grant nothing. No code, module URL, regex supplied by the contract, eval, dynamic import, user-authored expression or plugin callback. New source pins may be structurally valid but remain non-executable until independently admitted; identical model shape is not semantic approval.

P1 returns a diagnostic or unpadded ASCII decimal only for positive safe native JS integers with exact round-trip; preserve raw value/type. No numeric strings, booleans, fractions, zero, negative, rounding or target normalization. P2 checks presence/type/null/empty independently, country `[A-Z]{2}`, nonempty admin1 without a dot, and exact concatenation; preserves `01`, `x84`, whitespace and `00`. `exact-string/1` never trims/coerces and supplies no broader user-country permission. The accepted P1/P2 definitions are normative inputs, not new semantic proposals.

Graph references use full immutable references even when a selected source revision belongs to the outer provider repository: attachment-only publication may be newer than unchanged native artifacts. Use a graph-only explicit dependency resolver keyed by repository/revision; it may read another immutable revision of the same repository after checking identity. Do not relax the old `read`/`referenceFile` own-versus-external checks. Absolute source refs must all resolve to one selected native revision per source. Runtime provider revision may be a later admitted attachment-only revision; admission must bind it to these identical model/binding/data/native snapshot bytes.

## Pin validation and bounded proof

1. Parse strict UTF-8 JSON, reject duplicate keys/trailing data, maintain depth 32 and 2 MiB attachment maximum. One graph, two native source descriptors, six public stages, five extension edges, max two input fields per edge, max two grain fields, one optional branch. Keep reference path/repository/hash constraints; graph ID is a literal capability enum.
2. Graph metadata resolution has a distinct metadata budget: at most 32 unique files, 2 MiB per file, 8 MiB aggregate, one-level legacy/entry only. Ref cache is keyed by complete immutable tuple. Stop before an additional read would exceed the budget; no automatic network provisioning, redirects, branch refs or symlinks. These are proposed caps for this graph path, not wider metadata-default changes. Count the actual fixture closure before accepting implementation; do not quietly raise bounds if it fails.
3. Resolve entry document and exact contract index; verify the full original source/schema/data-if-present/namespace/decision and original eight-row selected fixture unchanged. Entry target must equal graph ROR organizations model/native snapshot/data. Existing entry eligibility plus graph eligibility are both necessary; no fallback through fixture-only Geo country contract.
4. Resolve both models, bindings and snapshot metadata. Every stage field/grain must exist. Preserve model-native references: ROR `locations.organization_id` declares `entity: organizations`, not a `type:string`; resolve that entity's one required key to prove wire type. Do not edit the model to appease the old property helper. Type checking must be graph-specific and bounded, with only this one-hop reference and cycle refusal. Grain equals declared ordered ModelSpec key; ordinal zero is valid.
5. Verify native decoded SQLite descriptor hashes against selected snapshot artifacts, model/binding closure and generation provenance; do not fetch giant SQLite as metadata. The accepted snapshot envelope is the actual source/artifact-snapshot.json, with real generator/artifacts and decoded descriptor. No full keyset download or invented native single-key receipt for composite locations. Reuse the existing native preparation/inventory selected-table proof to establish actual serving key uniqueness and native declared key uniqueness for the six public stages. Extend its checked proof output to include the exact graph closure/hash and native key/cardinality facts; proof is pinned evidence, never self-admission. No new public generic receipt schema is required for a browser runtime optimization: until such proof is independently admitted, all ordinary-page uniqueness stays unresolved.
6. Full-source duplicate/native type/ordinal/order proof is once per immutable prepared snapshot, using existing read-only preparation/native comparison, not per browser action. Check locations composite key and alias primary key separately from nonunique lookup fields. Do not demand FK totality: the accepted missing-place/admin1 sets remain legitimate visible exceptions. Response duplicate identity, type or unique-key contradictions invalidate the affected stage and halt its descendants; never pick first.
7. All graph operators, stage maps, requested alias option, selected input page, resolved entry/legacy refs, canonical indexes, meaning/binding/decision refs, native snapshots and four runtime pins participate in stable plan identity. Extend existing saved scenario with a graph-specific discriminated member; keep legacy shape unchanged. Saving copies verified graph bytes/ID and all resolved refs; revalidation checks each stage, not just the original user source. A saved `eligible` boolean or cached parsed graph never grants authority. Unknown format on any older reader fails closed.

Metadata validation and independently admitted execution remain separate, exactly as current contracts. `decision.document` authenticates the selected evidence file, not the meaning of words inside it. Publisher/Directory/app must all understand and independently gate the explicit graph member. The current default-activation publisher r3 repair (`c373a4…`, root-supplied) and companion goldens can land separately before this feature; this proposal neither edits their formats nor requires rebasing their work onto graph support.

## Execution and completeness

Keep `FederatedQueryService → federated-query.worker.ts → runFederatedQuery` and the admitted ordinary transport. Add a graph branch selected only after graph admission. Reuse frozen candidate `createImmutableFederationFetch`, `readPage`, `RuntimeReadReport`, `BoundedRunBudget`, `runtimePlanIdentity` and `saveRuntimePins` concepts after their pending repairs pass. Their current types are insufficient: replace graph-path source-array positional semantics with checked stage IDs/edge IDs and ordered input fields. Preserve legacy two-to-four-stage validator behavior; the new graph path alone permits seven stages.

The transport issues `parseDTQL`-validated ordinary single-collection `In` pages with exact derived strings, no caller ordering, no snapshot headers. There is one shared cache by `(source pins, database, collection, filter fingerprint, page)` and a separate parent-occurrence mapping. Fetch-key deduplication does not merge affiliations or location occurrences. Cache-native fields unchanged. Derived columns live in a separate app-owned relation (e.g. occurrence token, lookup key, diagnostics); do not inject a guessed reserved field into provider rows. DALgo `key` identifies local derived records without confusing native/serving keys.

DALgo reuse at installed 0.2.0: `parseDTQL`, `QueryExecutor.query(StructuredQuery)`, `QueryPage`, `executeJoinedDTQLQuery`, `executeJoinedDTQLQueryPages`, `JoinedQueryExecutionOptions.resolveSource`, `resolveExecutor`, `scanPages`, and IndexedDbDatabase transactions already compose local exact joins. `executeRecordLookups`/`executeRecordLookupPages` expose `keyOf`, `fetch`, `merge`, `signal` but are one-result-per-input APIs; do not use their merge to flatten multi-location/alias children. Resolve organization/location and each place singleton branch over local caches, after classifying invalid/ambiguous references. Build aliases as their own relation. No generic DALgo API change is mandatory. Join options have no AbortSignal: shared counters/admission before each cache operation/output chunk plus existing Worker hard cancellation are mandatory; options alone cannot prove 10s cancellation. Never silently substitute a hand-written Cartesian join engine.

Completion is tracked per `(edge, source/target pins, ordered eligible distinct key-set fingerprint, query fields, requested range/order profile)`, not per database or last page. A stage read is exhaustive only after contiguous ordinary pages from offset zero for that exact filter end with fewer rows than the actual requested limit. A full page is possibly-more; no sentinel request. An absent key from an incomplete batch is unresolved. A singleton seen on a partial page is still provisional unless an independent admitted exact-snapshot uniqueness proof covers that target key; for the minimal implementation conservatively wait for exhaustive coverage. Two observed distinct target rows for a unique key suffice for ambiguity even when further pages remain; preserve bounded witnesses and mark the total unknown. Many-side children observed on partial pages are visible with incomplete enumeration, never ambiguous merely for being plural.

Continuation is an explicit action on a named stage/range. It retains the original 10s deadline and cumulative budgets/pins; expiry requires a fresh explicit run. Before fetch, validate the exact saved active-run plan identity and remaining allowance. No automatic parent-page drainage, retry, branch continuation or cascading downstream network work. Materialized results may recompute locally after the explicit page, with budget charge. A changed parent eligible-key-set invalidates dependent filter coverage transitively; refuse continuation of its old child stream and require an explicit fresh run, as the candidate's conservative rule does. A parent extension whose deduplicated eligible set is unchanged may reuse immutable child coverage, but restores/charges every new occurrence. A sibling country continuation must not invalidate unchanged admin1/alias coverage. Changing requested aliases, projected fields, graph/operator/pins or selection makes a new plan and requires fresh explicit run. Retain old results as historical, never relabel them current.

Partial organization results retain all user parents. Zero locations is definitive only after the locations edge is exhaustive. Missing place retains affiliation, organization/status and location. A missing or incomplete admin1 never removes country/place; aliases never multiply singleton sibling results. A later response changing any of provider revision, source SQLite, serving SQLite or manifest hash refuses before local merge and halts all affected database stages. Server/Worker/direct/keyed route guards and selected-table boundaries remain exactly the prior accepted runtime/serving architecture obligations.

## Result grains, counters and resource accounting

Primary grid remains affiliations: one row per original key/token, including duplicate ROR references. Location context is a related set keyed by structured tuple `(affiliation token, ROR snapshot, organization_id, ordinal)`; it carries organization status, raw integer, derived place key, place/country/admin1 values plus separate edge diagnostics. A no-location affiliation has a parent status, never a fabricated ordinal. Aliases are a related set keyed by `(location-context tuple, Geo snapshot, alternate_name_id)` and preserve every native field including language, flags and periods. Parent/location linkage is explicit. Native records and serving record keys remain separate.

Extend `FederatedQueryResult` with bounded named related recordsets and their relation metadata rather than replacing `RunQueryResponse.recordset`. Existing result remains the affiliation grid. Extend Worker/service storage/page messages to carry result-set ID; use the current owned IndexedDB lifecycle and cleanup. Each set uses scalar typed columns and separate provenance/status descriptors; the existing `typed()` rejects arbitrary object values, so do not pretend nested JSON automatically works. UI renders primary and related grids through the existing result components; no silent flat alias expansion in this slice. If later requested, flat alias expansion is a separately explicit view preserving placeholders, composite keys and multiplication counts.

Every edge reports input occurrences, missing/null/empty/invalid/unsupported keys, eligible occurrences, distinct requested keys, matched/unmatched/ambiguous/incomplete/unattempted parent occurrences, child rows and multiplied parents. Root summary stays an affiliation denominator; no DISTINCT repair. Evidence truncation has its own explicit flag and leaves unresolved status where proof is insufficient. An exact lookup-key count is not an affiliation count.

Shared hard ceilings remain 10s monotonic deadline, 1000 selected users, 50 distinct ROR IDs, 100 distinct place IDs, 5000 intermediate rows, 5000 output rows, 5 MiB cumulative decoded network and separate 5 MiB materialized output. Derived country/admin1 key sets cannot exceed the 100 admitted places. All six edges, error bodies, failed reads, cached input, intermediate derived/occurrence relations, duplicate fan-out, placeholders, provenance and all related resultsets share accounting. Count source rows and added derived/occurrence rows against one cumulative intermediate-work ledger; count final row/provenance bytes across all sets simultaneously. Replacements charge retained output deltas atomically while processing work still spends cumulative intermediate allowance. Do not reset per set, branch, cache, continuation or DALgo invocation. Before expansion, reserve row/byte allowance including at least bounded incomplete markers; if the next record/witness cannot fit, retain existing bounded evidence and mark affected branch incomplete without allocating oversized data. Rejected over-budget chunk never becomes visible. The exact 5MiB serialization estimator must equal the bytes of emitted typed values/metadata, not deduplicated source data.

DALgo `maxFetchedRows`, `maxResultRows`, `maxCandidateEvaluations`, `maxRetainedBytes` supplement these run-level ledgers. Pass remaining budgets, refuse zero before invoking DALgo (never let zero choose defaults), and cap cumulative candidate evaluations at the existing 100000 default across all branch calls. Local scan cache hits spend processing/retention allowance but not fictitious HTTP bytes. An explicit no-action control must prove no network calls. Observed exhaustion yields visible incomplete/deferred work, not unmatched or hidden dropped parents.

## Mandatory owners and verification matrix

| Owner / minimal files | Required extension | Decisive tests |
|---|---|---|
| OVDB publisher `publisher/representation/schema4.json`, new graph.go/tests; contract.go format dispatch, schema registry tests; internal/publisher/repo/representation.go dependency/graph-check integration | separate graph parse/check; one-level original-format legacy/entry delegation; bounded explicit dependency refs and entity-reference resolution | formats1/2/3 existing goldens byte/verdict unchanged; schema identities coexist; unknown formats/operators/topologies/fields, cycles, hashes and missing dependency refuse; no giant data fetch |
| Directory `schemas/representation/schema4.json`, `scripts/lib/representation.mjs`, `scripts/test-representation.mjs` and caller fixture corpus | identical new schema/hash and graph structural/metadata admission path; old companion remains unchanged in meaning | cross-language golden agreement for positive/hostile graph closure, same-repo older pin, malformed legacy/entry, duplicate keys and budget overflow |
| DataTug hub existing `spec/research/public-data-fabric/evidence/` | publish exact accepted P1/P2/P3 decision and review/acceptance pins through root lane | scratch accepted hashes preserved; committed decision hash known before replacing UNPUBLISHED tokens; no user fixture widening |
| Geo provider existing attachment/snapshot metadata; existing model/meaning registration and Directory entry owners | new graph envelope plus exact legacy ref; selected models/native data unchanged; update attachment-only pins and graph metadata closure | rehash native SQLite/models/bindings/fixture; preserve current source selection and all existing bridge cases; graph closure resolves entry and both selected providers |
| Existing Cloud/preparation owner | graph-specific native grain/uniqueness verification in current preparation evidence; reuse selected-table inventory/four-pin guards | compare native composite keys/ordinals/status; target uniqueness, repeated-location synthetic and missing-reference exceptions; hidden tables remain inaccessible; no new API route |
| App `representation-discovery.ts`, new graph-contract.ts/schema4; public-data.service.ts, public-data-scenario.ts, saved-plan-revalidation.ts | separate graph admission and saved scenario member; retain original entry; exact per-stage pin check | unknown capability cannot execute via saved booleans/config; all graph edits invalidate saved identity; old scenarios unchanged; reopen/check without action remains idle |
| App candidate `immutable-federation.ts`, `bounded-federation.ts`, `bounded-run-budget.ts`, new native-graph-executor.ts; federated-query-executor/service/worker/storage; query-def.ts | stage/edge filters, typed projection, related sets, branch coverage, shared ledger integrated in existing executor | real installed DALgo path, P1/P2 counterexamples, partial/full pages, changed parent filters, sibling independence, cap/expiry/cancel/error/cache accounting, no extra request |
| App public-data-page component and existing result-page consumer; saved-runtime-pins.ts | related grids and explicit named continuation; save every graph/runtime pin | browser J1–J6; distinct parents; no cross products; changed pin409; real transport/Worker/driver cancellation; all-status/multi-location/aliases visibility |

Mandatory integrated semantic controls are the accepted exact eight affiliation rows (3 matched references to 2 organizations, 1 NULL, 1 empty, 3 invalid; no unmatched/ambiguous), plus separate synthetic/real multiplicity controls. Real `https://ror.org/0042xzm63` with two affiliations gives four location rows and 76 alias child rows, never 384. Keep nine missing place IDs/59 location occurrences, 234 Geo place admin1 exceptions across 78 keys, 56 empty admin1, `MC.00` matched and `VN.x84` unmatched as separately scoped offline facts; do not confuse their denominators with bounded user runs. Duplicate target keys cause ambiguity, duplicate child primary keys cause integrity failure, distinct alias rows are legitimate multiplicity. Test missing/wrong field native types and impossible rounded P1 values without changing approved inputs.

Independent architecture review must challenge this packet before implementation assignment. Subsequent implementation has independent tests/review, canonical admission and real browser/runtime/Directory J1–J6 gates. This packet establishes no live capacity, default publisher activation, runtime availability or whole-wave acceptance. No DALgo release, Go runtime endpoint, canonical model rewrite, registry redesign or selection expansion is intrinsically required by this graph addition; inherited runtime fixes remain prerequisites.

## Compatibility, publication order and practical UI

The format 4 wrapper deliberately has no top-level `contracts` array. Old `Parse` falls through to the format 1 schema, which rejects its format constant and unknown members. Old Directory `schemaPins` rejects the unknown format; old app schema routing rejects it too. Required regression: give each unchanged old reader a graph wrapper whose referenced legacy contract is individually valid, and prove the **whole wrapper is refused with zero data reads**. No reader may salvage its legacy reference, select the old ROR entry alone, or show a graph-enabled suggestion after rejection. Separately prove the original format 1/2/3 documents still pass unchanged with identical SHA256/proof results. References may preserve old bytes at the existing old path; no byte reserialization is required.

Publication is staged: land the independently repairable current publisher/companion work; land schema4 and validators with graph eligibility still closed; land app graph execution/UX behind the same closed canonical admission; publish the committed decision and attachment-only provider artifacts after independent review; update existing registry/Directory pins only once every required current consumer passes the exact graph fixture. Mixed deployments containing old consumers refuse graph discovery/execution. Unsupported graph must not authorize fallback queries; existing separately selected old scenarios remain old scenarios. A new operator/graph capability requires another reviewed release/admission, never a remotely enabled boolean.

Manifest association is exact at every stage. Admission maps each graph `(source native snapshot/model/data, entity)` to the admitted provider/publisher manifest selected collection and checked immutable runtime database. There must be exactly one selected serving collection for that physical entity, and its native field/grain semantics must agree with the manifest schema. Source snapshot pins and model hash do not prove deployment selection alone. Persist the admitted publisher manifest ref/hash and recordset mapping in the saved graph stage pins, plus the runtime manifest SHA256 received with provider/source/serving pins. Refuse changed collection selection, field type/coercion, serving-key map, busy timeout or snapshot association even if the SQLite data bytes are unchanged. The runtime manifest hash must identify the exact verified bytes used to mount; the source revision header alone never substitutes. Follow the existing native-table serving boundary: no hidden diagnostics, no broad all-table fallback. This integration reuses the existing manifest inventory/admission evidence, not a second deployment registry.

J1/J2 discovery only reads permitted metadata within the graph metadata budget; neither native SQLite, compressed pieces, user `source.data`, nor a target record is read. Source-byte/input-fixture proof is performed by existing offline publication validation or explicit run preparation, not auto-fetch while discovering. Actual user lookup remains behind explicit Run and both entry/graph admission; a query-shaped graph config in a saved plan cannot bypass the existing `definition.publicData` real-query gate. The gate changes only after canonical publication and review, with a single shared predicate used by visible actions and Worker/executor checks.

UI labels are **Affiliations**, **Locations — each affiliation's organization locations**, and **Alternate names — names for each location**. Show organization status and independent Place/Country/Region/Aliases statuses in Locations; use “Region (GeoNames admin1)” in its explanation rather than claiming ISO subdivision identity. Show “No locations” on its affiliation, and “More rows available”, “Incomplete”, “Not requested” or an invalid-reference explanation where appropriate. Aliases is off unless explicitly selected before Run; checking it after a run prepares a new run, never a silent fetch. The related views open/focus existing locally materialized rows without network work; “Load next page” names the source/branch and remaining ability to continue. Source revisions/operator identifiers belong in expandable provenance and saved details, not the main flow. Do not display a settled zero/unmatched count for incomplete coverage. No flat alias view is part of this slice.

# W1 native projection contract architecture — proposal r2

Status: **architecture repair r2 for fresh independent re-review; no implementation or admission**. M1/M2/M3 accepted and repaired below; none declined. Frozen r1 files remain unchanged. Local Codex/macOS, 2026-10-05. Root is sole lander. P1/P2/P3 are accepted inputs, not reconciled again here. No repository or author worktree was modified.

## Journey and recommendation

J1: I select my already accepted `Affiliation.ror_id` field and discover organization context from admitted metadata. Good result: explanation identifies the exact user contract, raw field, native sources and checked projection; no data lookup. J2: I inspect the organization → ordered locations → place graph, its independent country/admin1 branches and optional aliases. Good result: scope, attribution, multiplicity and bounds are visible. J3: I explicitly run it. Good result: bounded ordinary reads produce distinct affiliation, location and alias grains. J4: I inspect matched, invalid, unmatched, ambiguous and incomplete outcomes without losing parents. J5: I save, reopen, check changed metadata and explicitly continue or rerun. Good result: every graph/stage/operator/source/runtime pin is retained; changed pins require review; reopening is idle. J6: I decline, wait or cancel. Good result: no implicit request, and cancellation terminates active work.

Recommend a **separate, closed native graph member** in an additive `ovdb-representation-contract/4` attachment envelope. Keep the existing `representation_contract: {path, sha256}` publisher/Directory link. The new envelope has one optional local `legacy` reference to the existing unchanged format 1/2/3 document and exactly one graph. This is a one-level composition, never a recursive import system. The graph executes only this accepted source-qualified W1 topology. Keep the existing ROR user contract and every legacy contract byte unchanged; do not widen native-identifier or replace its decision pin. Publish the accepted new decision in the existing DataTug evidence area and reference it from the graph's existing-shaped `decision` field, but never treat its prose as executable authority.

Use related result sets inside the existing DataTug query/service/Worker path: affiliations, location context, alias children. Reuse DALgo exact joins over bounded local caches; projection produces app-owned derived rows alongside native data. Do not add a generic expression language, server relational execution, new dataset registry or fresh Geo selection.

## Exact evidence and why existing mechanisms are insufficient

All repository claims here refer to exact Git objects, **not fresh remote-head claims**. The supplied app candidate is frozen r1 patch, not the author's repairing worktree. `source-evidence.json` records exact extracted bytes/hashes. Inspected:

- OVDB publisher `27f2664782e01feb4fb5938f28b8f8eae0a868a8`, released baseline supplied by root; `publisher/representation/{schema.json,schema2.json,schema3.json,contract.go,native.go,attachment.go,strict.go}`.
- App `413bb772e04f139210adec92ad0cb3fce2b07883`; frozen `artifact:data-fabric-w1-app-bounded-runtime/candidate-r1.patch`. Candidate known budget findings are not accepted or repeated as solved here.
- DALgo JS `1534acd4d0e4a104c58eba09fb9c25619efc8f24`, package version 0.2.0; app package.json selects that exact revision.
- Directory companion cached object `d946bd032b31d590fce0ebafc56537c0b77dcfad`, `scripts/lib/representation.mjs`; no current-remote assertion.
- ROR `dc78c1e929f1f10018f8c39e690351059a50c71f`, native SQLite `afdf9781…d5d38`, model `9694a0b6…ae`; Geo `6f4cf1269bc393048f6b204069135a62f0bb6c02`, native SQLite `cb53af14…456d`, model `609fe73e…81`. Exact full values in example/evidence. No newer Geo candidate is selected.

| Existing surface | Actual checked behavior | Consequence |
|---|---|---|
| Format 1 | closed label bridge; string single-property source; identity transform; zero-or-one | cannot represent native integer P1, two-component P2, or reverse enumeration |
| Format 2 | closed discriminated label-bridge/native-identifier; native equal namespaces, string source/target; required single-property target key | native location composite identity and integer-to-string projection cannot be passed as native identity |
| Format 3 | native only, adds exact external source.data; all identity restrictions remain | source.data provides artifact identity, not new operations |
| `Check`, `checkNative`, `checkSnapshot` | external source schema, provider-local target/native files, duplicate single source refusal, single target key and native receipt association | blanket loosening would silently change old contract semantics |
| `ParseAttachment` and Directory envelope | exactly local JSON path and SHA256 | natural extension point; no manifest field is needed |
| `decision.document` | immutable external file bytes verified; app explicitly says provenance, not a free-prose acceptance parser | cannot hide an operator/approval in prose |
| App `SourceField`, `PublicDataScenario` | datatype string; saved projection identity; one attachment/model/decision | need additive graph-specific saved pins, not fabricated string model |
| `BoundedSource`, `validateBounds` | one parent field, two-to-four stages; candidate loads string filter values | cannot produce P1/P2; seven-stage branch cannot be claimed as a linear plan |
| DALgo DTQL | equality join fields and arithmetic expression variants; no arbitrary conversion/composite callback in query model | a SQL/DTQL cast or ad-hoc callback in saved text neither carries authority nor validates source pins |
| Saved query/runtime pins | persist query/projection/bounds and four runtime pins | useful storage, insufficient authority until graph attachment is checked/admitted |

Rejected alternatives: changing native source datatypes; accepting all numbers in current string path; putting transformation rules in decision prose; a generated string column in the canonical source model; a new global transform registry. A graph only inside user-editable `federation` would be an unadmitted authority. A separate manifest graph field would duplicate the existing attachment machinery. An additive format is required because old schema `additionalProperties:false` and transform/cardinality constants must keep rejecting these changes.

## Minimal serialized extension

`contract-example-r2.json` is the concrete serialized design template. It includes exact selected native refs and every physical edge. Values beginning `UNPUBLISHED_` deliberately fail validation: the accepted scratch decision has no committed immutable decision pin yet. The example now names the exact existing ROR format 3 entry at 24bcbcb5 and exact unchanged Geo legacy bytes at 57e25689; the outer graph wrapper and final admission revisions remain unpublished. Do not invent those hashes or use the app fixture as canonical publication. The outer Geo publisher will point its existing attachment field to a new file, e.g. `representation-graph.json`. `legacy` points at the unchanged previous Geo attachment JSON at that same outer provider revision. ROR's attachment stays unchanged and is referenced as the graph entry.

Envelope keys are exactly `format`, optional `legacy`, and `graphs`. `legacy` is a single local path/SHA reference, never self-reference; its document must be format 1, 2 or 3 and passes the existing checker with its original format and outer provider context. No format 4 nested dependency is allowed. The graph entry attachment is likewise limited to one exact format 2/3 document and one `contractIndex`, checked against full selected source and target identity; no recursive graph resolution. In particular, the new document is **not** a mixed array that retrospectively reinterprets older contracts under format 4.

Graph keys and enums are closed, as in the example. `execution=native-graph`, `id=w1-ror-geonames-context/1`, `resultShape=affiliations-location-context-aliases/1` are finite checked capabilities. `sources` has exactly `ror` and `geo`; `stages` has exactly six public stages plus the existing entry's user stage; `edges` has exactly the five additional edges below (six total with entry). Aliases is the sole optional requested branch. Unknown members, IDs, topology, operators, additional fields/edges, cycles, backward edges or duplicate IDs fail before any data request. This finite implementation is not a generic graph interpreter.

| From → to | Raw fields → lookup field | Projection | Cardinality/grain |
|---|---|---|---|
| Existing user → organizations | `Affiliation.ror_id` → `id` | original admitted ROR contract | zero-or-one; affiliation parent |
| organizations → locations | `id` → `organization_id` | `exact-string/1` | zero-or-many; `(organization_id,ordinal)` |
| locations → places | `geonames_id:int` → `geonameid:string` | `ror-positive-int-geonames-decimal/1` | zero-or-one |
| places → countries | `country_code` → `iso` | `exact-string/1` | zero-or-one |
| places → admin1 | ordered `(country_code,admin1_code)` → `code` | `geonames-country-admin1/1` | zero-or-one |
| places → aliases | `geonameid` → `geonameid` | `exact-string/1` | zero-or-many; `alternate_name_id` |

Dispatch is a closed switch over `(graph capability, edge ID, ordered source fields/types, source model/dataset hashes, target fields/types/model/dataset hashes, operator version)`, derived from the checked graph. IDs alone grant nothing. No code, module URL, regex supplied by the contract, eval, dynamic import, user-authored expression or plugin callback. New source pins may be structurally valid but remain non-executable until independently admitted; identical model shape is not semantic approval.

P1 returns a diagnostic or unpadded ASCII decimal only for positive safe native JS integers with exact round-trip; preserve raw value/type. No numeric strings, booleans, fractions, zero, negative, rounding or target normalization. P2 checks presence/type/null/empty independently, country `[A-Z]{2}`, nonempty admin1 without a dot, and exact concatenation; preserves `01`, `x84`, whitespace and `00`. `exact-string/1` never trims/coerces and supplies no broader user-country permission. The accepted P1/P2 definitions are normative inputs, not new semantic proposals.

Graph references use full immutable references even when a selected source revision belongs to the outer provider repository: attachment-only publication may be newer than unchanged native artifacts. Use a graph-only explicit dependency resolver keyed by repository/revision; it may read another immutable revision of the same repository after checking identity. Do not relax the old `read`/`referenceFile` own-versus-external checks. Absolute source refs must all resolve to one selected native revision per source. Runtime provider revision may be a later admitted attachment-only revision; admission must bind it to these identical model/binding/data/native snapshot bytes.

## Pin validation and bounded proof

1. Parse strict UTF-8 JSON, reject duplicate keys/trailing data, maintain depth 32 and 2 MiB attachment maximum. One graph, two native source descriptors, six public stages, five extension edges, max two input fields per edge, max two grain fields, one optional branch. Keep reference path/repository/hash constraints; graph ID is a literal capability enum.
2. The entire metadata operation uses the existing **2 MiB aggregate, 96 unique immutable references, reference ancestry depth 8** reader. Remove r1's separate 8 MiB allowance and unmeasured 32-file cap. The same reader accounts canonical indexes, graph wrapper, legacy/entry documents and their actual dependencies, source metadata, decisions, attribution and admission/manifest evidence. A cache hit spends its bytes once per operation; repeated references to the same complete tuple in the same operation reuse that admission. Stream each response against remaining bytes; failed/invalid bytes cannot create a fresh allowance. Abort this graph metadata operation on any metadata-fetch failure; do not catch it and continue with a fresh reader or uncharged error-body retry. One-level graph composition still applies independently of the depth-8 reader. See measured closure and unpublished holes below; final closure must fit before publication, with no automatic cap increase.
3. Resolve entry document and exact contract index; verify the full original source/schema/data-if-present/namespace/decision and original eight-row selected fixture unchanged. Entry target must equal graph ROR organizations model/native snapshot/data. Existing entry eligibility plus graph eligibility are both necessary; no fallback through fixture-only Geo country contract.
4. Resolve both models, bindings and snapshot metadata. Every stage field/grain must exist. Preserve model-native references: ROR `locations.organization_id` declares `entity: organizations`, not a `type:string`; resolve that entity's one required key to prove wire type. Do not edit the model to appease the old property helper. Type checking must be graph-specific and bounded, with only this one-hop reference and cycle refusal. Grain equals declared ordered ModelSpec key; ordinal zero is valid.
5. Verify native decoded SQLite descriptor hashes against selected snapshot artifacts, model/binding closure and generation provenance; do not fetch giant SQLite as metadata. The accepted snapshot envelope is the actual source/artifact-snapshot.json, with real generator/artifacts and decoded descriptor. No full keyset download or invented native single-key receipt for composite locations. Reuse the existing native preparation/inventory selected-table proof to establish actual serving key uniqueness and native declared key uniqueness for the six public stages. Extend its checked proof output to include the exact graph closure/hash and native key/cardinality facts; proof is pinned evidence, never self-admission. No new public generic receipt schema is required for a browser runtime optimization: until such proof is independently admitted, all ordinary-page uniqueness stays unresolved.
6. Full-source duplicate/native type/ordinal/order proof is once per immutable prepared snapshot, using existing read-only preparation/native comparison, not per browser action. Check locations composite key and alias primary key separately from nonunique lookup fields. Do not demand FK totality: the accepted missing-place/admin1 sets remain legitimate visible exceptions. Response duplicate identity, type or unique-key contradictions invalidate the affected stage and halt its descendants; never pick first.
7. All graph operators, stage maps, requested alias option, selected input page, resolved entry/legacy refs, canonical indexes, meaning/binding/decision refs, native snapshots and four runtime pins participate in stable plan identity. Extend existing saved scenario with a graph-specific discriminated member; keep legacy shape unchanged. Saving copies verified graph bytes/ID and all resolved refs; revalidation checks each stage, not just the original user source. A saved `eligible` boolean or cached parsed graph never grants authority. Unknown format on any older reader fails closed.

Metadata validation and independently admitted execution remain separate, exactly as current contracts. `decision.document` authenticates the selected evidence file, not the meaning of words inside it. Publisher/Directory/app must all understand and independently gate the explicit graph member. The current default-activation publisher r3 repair (`c373a4…`, root-supplied) and companion goldens can land separately before this feature; this proposal neither edits their formats nor requires rebasing their work onto graph support.

## Execution and completeness

Keep `FederatedQueryService → federated-query.worker.ts → runFederatedQuery` and the admitted ordinary transport. Add a graph branch selected only after graph admission. Reuse frozen candidate `createImmutableFederationFetch`, `readPage`, `RuntimeReadReport`, `BoundedRunBudget`, `runtimePlanIdentity` and `saveRuntimePins` concepts after their pending repairs pass. Their current types are insufficient: replace graph-path source-array positional semantics with checked stage IDs/edge IDs and ordered input fields. Preserve legacy two-to-four-stage validator behavior; the new graph path alone permits seven stages.

The transport issues `parseDTQL`-validated ordinary single-collection `In` pages with exact derived strings, no caller ordering, no snapshot headers. There is one shared cache by `(source pins, database, collection, filter fingerprint, page)` and a separate parent-occurrence mapping. Fetch-key deduplication does not merge affiliations or location occurrences. Cache-native fields unchanged. Derived columns live in a separate app-owned relation (e.g. occurrence token, lookup key, diagnostics); do not inject a guessed reserved field into provider rows. DALgo `key` identifies local derived records without confusing native/serving keys.

DALgo reuse at installed 0.2.0: `parseDTQL`, `QueryExecutor.query(StructuredQuery)`, `QueryPage`, `executeJoinedDTQLQuery`, `executeJoinedDTQLQueryPages`, `JoinedQueryExecutionOptions.resolveSource`, `resolveExecutor`, `scanPages`, and IndexedDbDatabase transactions already compose local exact joins. `executeRecordLookups`/`executeRecordLookupPages` expose `keyOf`, `fetch`, `merge`, `signal` but are one-result-per-input APIs; do not use their merge to flatten multi-location/alias children. Resolve organization/location and each place singleton branch over local caches, after classifying invalid/ambiguous references. Build aliases as their own relation. No generic DALgo API change is mandatory. The r2 finite materialized hash plan below is the only permitted DALgo path for this graph; do not use paged/aggregate execution here. Join options have no AbortSignal: admission before each cache operation/output chunk plus existing Worker hard cancellation remain mandatory; these probes do not prove 10s product cancellation. No generic DALgo API change is required for the proved finite path.

Completion is tracked per `(edge, source/target pins, ordered eligible distinct key-set fingerprint, query fields, requested range/order profile)`, not per database or last page. A stage read is exhaustive only after contiguous ordinary pages from offset zero for that exact filter end with fewer rows than the actual requested limit. A full page is possibly-more; no sentinel request. An absent key from an incomplete batch is unresolved. A singleton seen on a partial page is still provisional unless an independent admitted exact-snapshot uniqueness proof covers that target key; for the minimal implementation conservatively wait for exhaustive coverage. Two observed distinct target rows for a unique key suffice for ambiguity even when further pages remain; preserve bounded witnesses and mark the total unknown. Many-side children observed on partial pages are visible with incomplete enumeration, never ambiguous merely for being plural.

Continuation is an explicit action on a named stage/range. It retains the original 10s deadline and cumulative budgets/pins; expiry requires a fresh explicit run. Before fetch, validate the exact saved active-run plan identity and remaining allowance. No automatic parent-page drainage, retry, branch continuation or cascading downstream network work. Materialized results may recompute locally after the explicit page, with budget charge. A changed parent eligible-key-set invalidates dependent filter coverage transitively; refuse continuation of its old child stream and require an explicit fresh run, as the candidate's conservative rule does. A parent extension whose deduplicated eligible set is unchanged may reuse immutable child coverage, but restores/charges every new occurrence. A sibling country continuation must not invalidate unchanged admin1/alias coverage. Changing requested aliases, projected fields, graph/operator/pins or selection makes a new plan and requires fresh explicit run. Retain old results as historical, never relabel them current.

Partial organization results retain all user parents. Zero locations is definitive only after the locations edge is exhaustive. Missing place retains affiliation, organization/status and location. A missing or incomplete admin1 never removes country/place; aliases never multiply singleton sibling results. A later response changing any of provider revision, source SQLite, serving SQLite or manifest hash refuses before local merge and halts all affected database stages. Server/Worker/direct/keyed route guards and selected-table boundaries remain exactly the prior accepted runtime/serving architecture obligations.

## Result grains, counters and resource accounting

Primary grid remains affiliations: one row per original key/token, including duplicate ROR references. Location context is a related set keyed by structured tuple `(affiliation token, ROR snapshot, organization_id, ordinal)`; it carries organization status, raw integer, derived place key, place/country/admin1 values plus separate edge diagnostics. A no-location affiliation has a parent status, never a fabricated ordinal. Aliases are a related set keyed by `(location-context tuple, Geo snapshot, alternate_name_id)` and preserve every native field including language, flags and periods. Parent/location linkage is explicit. Native records and serving record keys remain separate.

Extend `FederatedQueryResult` with bounded named related recordsets and their relation metadata rather than replacing `RunQueryResponse.recordset`. Existing result remains the affiliation grid. Extend Worker/service storage/page messages to carry result-set ID; use the current owned IndexedDB lifecycle and cleanup. Each set uses scalar typed columns and separate provenance/status descriptors; the existing `typed()` rejects arbitrary object values, so do not pretend nested JSON automatically works. UI renders primary and related grids through the existing result components; no silent flat alias expansion in this slice. If later requested, flat alias expansion is a separately explicit view preserving placeholders, composite keys and multiplication counts.

Every edge reports input occurrences, missing/null/empty/invalid/unsupported keys, eligible occurrences, distinct requested keys, matched/unmatched/ambiguous/incomplete/unattempted parent occurrences, child rows and multiplied parents. Root summary stays an affiliation denominator; no DISTINCT repair. Evidence truncation has its own explicit flag and leaves unresolved status where proof is insufficient. An exact lookup-key count is not an affiliation count.

Shared hard ceilings remain 10s monotonic deadline, 1000 selected users, 50 distinct ROR IDs, 100 distinct place IDs, 5000 cumulative materialized intermediate records, 5000 retained output rows across all related sets, 5 MiB cumulative decoded network and separate 5 MiB materialized output. The r2 event ledger below precisely defines materialized records versus repeat references/scans. It supersedes r1's ambiguous claim that every cached scan and all processing work consume another intermediate row. Fan-out, failed admitted work, replacement allocations, placeholders and provenance are charged as specified; no branch, continuation or engine invocation resets any counter. Derived country/admin1 sets remain bounded by 100 places.

The candidate ledger is app-owned and pre-debited from exact bounded multiplicities before the one permitted flat hash call. It never depends on DALgo returning its private counter. Candidate work has a separate cumulative 100000 ceiling, and row/byte admission remains independent. Exact mechanisms and witness receipts follow.
## Repair r2 M1 — measured metadata closure and remaining publication gate

`measure-closure-r2.py` reads exact Git objects and walks the actual four-contract Geo format 2 legacy and one-contract ROR format 3 entry references. `metadata-closure-r2.json` enumerates each immutable tuple, byte count, roles, depth and candidate status. It includes three exact baseline canonical indexes; legacy source models/bridge artifacts/key index/bindings/canonical meaning/decisions/snapshot; ROR source schema, target model/binding/meaning/decision/native provenance/snapshot; the graph's original selected native models/bindings/snapshots and generation/native-key evidence, including Geo's referenced original generation snapshot; attribution; and both exact candidate publisher manifests. It does **not** count the source-code review bundle, query SQLite/chunks, read the user affiliation data, or recursively download all artifacts named by a snapshot.

Known closure is **445186 bytes / 42 tuples**. Concrete provisional graph wrapper, accepted semantic-decision JSON and root acceptance bytes add **71185 bytes / 3 prospective tuples**. Total measured baseline is **516371 bytes / 45 references**, max ancestry 3. Remaining shared allowance is **1580781 bytes / 51 references**, with depth margin 5. Same bytes at different revisions count as different tuples; complete-tuple dedup is not content-hash-only dedup. The number 42 happens to match the former source-review count, but this is an independently enumerated browser-metadata list, not that bundle.

The final closure remains incomplete: final canonical-index revisions may change sizes; final graph wrapper and committed decision replace provisional bytes; final outer Geo revision changes the legacy tuple while preserving its bytes; final graph admission/collection mapping replaces or extends provisional acceptance; two generated runtime manifests and exact association refs are absent; any required public runtime descriptors/routes/licence docs have no final selected bytes; publisher manifests remain exact **local candidates**, Geo a10b7e89b6b0f76f915ad067043e251d5571182a and ROR 6f90dbc1093b77c3b4d1a3689bddb20c6007b62f. All new bytes, replacements' positive growth and new tuples share the stated remaining allowance. No final graph admission is inferred from spare room. Freeze all final refs and run the same closure walk before publication; refuse if it exceeds 2 MiB/96/depth8.

This measurement is for checking the selected W1 graph from its explicitly selected ROR entry, using the same reader from canonical-index load through graph admission. If the existing discover-all-provider loop performs additional metadata reads in that operation, those reads consume the **same remaining allowance**; the implementation must list them in the final closure or scope the graph check to this selected entry as a separate user-requested metadata operation. It cannot silently exclude them, reset the reader midway, or claim this baseline proves a wider discovery closure. These old index pins measure concrete current input bytes, not evidence that those indexes already contain the new graph.

## Repair r2 M2 — exact finite local plan and candidate debit

Only `executeJoinedDTQLQuery` materialized execution from the pinned DALgo 0.2.0 module is permitted. Build each call from the checked graph edge rather than accepting saved arbitrary DTQL: exactly two leaf relations, distinct aliases, exactly one left join, one direct cross-side `==` predicate, string lookup keys (including already checked P1/P2 derived keys), `hints.algorithms=['hash']`, no child joins, external correlations, derived queries, additional predicates, ordering, grouping, aggregates, filters, offsets, limit or `scanPages`. Columns are token references, not copies of provider payloads. Reject a shape mismatch before invoking DALgo. Invalid reference rows are diagnosed outside the join and retain their parent; ambiguous singleton key groups are never admitted for downstream expansion.

This integration reuses the existing manifest inventory/admission evidence, not a second deployment registry.

Source-byte/input-fixture proof is performed by existing offline publication validation or explicit run preparation, not auto-fetch while discovering. Actual user lookup remains behind explicit Run and both entry/graph admission; a query-shaped graph config in a saved plan cannot bypass the existing `definition.publicData` real-query gate. The gate changes only after canonical publication and review, with a single shared predicate used by visible actions and Worker/executor checks.

Show organization status and independent Place/Country/Region/Aliases statuses in Locations; use “Region (GeoNames admin1)” in its explanation rather than claiming ISO subdivision identity. Source revisions/operator identifiers belong in expandable provenance and saved details, not the main flow. Do not display a settled zero/unmatched count for incomplete coverage. # Native graph architecture independent review r1

**Verdict: repairs required before architecture acceptance or implementation assignment.** Three major findings; no semantic reconciliation reopening. Reviewer: fresh independent Codex agent, local macOS, 2026-10-05. Root remains sole lander. Only private scratch files were written.

Reviewed proposal MD SHA256 `2d323f8b933e2cb3a0923f6b58669ce742d65679fcb45f5a3831bc9502585770`, JSON SHA256 `912a2577d6db638b52bcb4ea1a4461920c1995ee5e542f8fd57fd9665e6a4640`, example SHA256 `bc32c94134c8c35f44da7a065f0e7c1520a33bba99840f8f50a23def144b4ccf`. All 42 source-evidence entries were independently read with `git show <exact revision>:<path>` and matched both recorded hashes and extracted bytes. These are exact-object findings, not remote-head/CI/publication claims.

## Findings

### M1 — Restore the accepted 2 MiB aggregate metadata budget and measure the complete closure

Location: proposal-r1.md:64; proposal-r1.json `limits.metadata_aggregate_bytes`.

The proposed 8 MiB graph allowance changes an accepted bound. Runtime architecture r3:164 explicitly requires metadata 2 MiB aggregate. App `canonical-metadata.ts:117–166` at both frozen `413bb772…` and supplied published candidate `65ebc741…` implements that aggregate bound, including reused cache bytes, with 96 references and reference depth 8. A separate graph path does not remove the changed contract. Root explicitly confirmed in this review that no increase is authorized.

Repair: keep **2 MiB for the entire discovery operation**, sharing the accounting across canonical indexes, wrapper, legacy document and its actual dependencies, entry document and dependencies, native graph metadata, decisions, and admission/manifest evidence. Measure and publish a deduplicated immutable-tuple closure list with per-file bytes, aggregate bytes, reference count and depth. The proposed 32-file cap also needs that measurement. Unpublished decision/entry/legacy pins mean final closure cannot yet be claimed complete; identify concrete provisional bytes and remaining slots rather than presenting 8 MiB as the default solution. If the actual closure cannot fit, return that measured incompatibility as an explicit unresolved architecture choice. Preserve streaming remaining-byte checks, cached-byte accounting and zero data lookup. Do not count the 42-file reviewer source bundle as the browser closure.

### M2 — Specify a cumulative candidate accounting mechanism that exists in DALgo 0.2.0

Location: proposal-r1.md:79,97. Evidence: pinned `src/join.ts:37–66,98–126,391–397`.

`maxCandidateEvaluations` is a per-invocation bound. Its counter is constructed privately as `{candidates:0}` and is never returned. `onProgress` reports downloaded/output row counts, which do not reveal candidate evaluations. Therefore “pass remaining budgets” does not establish how the remaining candidate allowance changes after a successful or failed invocation. Charging a returned row per candidate is incorrect; reserving the whole remaining allowance for each call prevents later branches.

Independent bounded execution used the exact pinned source, transpiled without source edits. A hash join and nested-loop join over the same 1000 input rows and 60 unique target rows returned identical 1000 rows and identical progress callbacks, while evaluator-derived counts are respectively 1000 and 60000. Two individually permitted nested-loop calls perform 120000 candidates. See `probe.mjs` and `probe-results.json`. This is an API accounting counterexample, not a claim that the proposed W1 implementation must choose nested-loop joins.

Repair: for this finite graph, specify exact permitted local join shape/algorithm and an app-owned **pre-execution debit** that bounds its candidates from the already bounded key multiplicities. For single equality hash edges, an explicit sum of parent occurrence count times matching child count can reserve candidates without a Cartesian join engine. State how unmatched placeholders, failed calls, recomputation and continuation are charged; show that actual evaluation cannot exceed the reservation, and never refund work already performed. Prove the permitted DALgo path actually uses the assumed algorithm and cannot silently fall back to a different shape. Alternatively propose a separately reviewed API change. The current blanket “no API change mandatory” claim is plausible only after this concrete mechanism is supplied.

### M3 — Define the intermediate ledger’s debit events and demonstrate useful ordinary capacity

Location: proposal-r1.md:95–97. Evidence: pinned `src/join.ts:323–356,369–409`.

“Source rows,” “added derived/occurrence rows,” “processing work” and “local scan cache hits” are assigned to one cumulative 5000-row ledger without an exact allocation/debit model. DALgo's fetched/result limits cap each invocation and retained intermediate arrays; they are not cumulative accounting for every stage's processing work. An implementer could charge a cached row at download, cache insertion, each local relation scan, derived-row creation and output projection, or only at selected events. These are materially different budgets.

A simple permitted input exposes the risk: 1000 affiliations referencing one organization with one location/place, aliases off, produces only 2000 retained rows across the affiliation/location sets. Five sequential occurrence-level joins (organization, locations, place, country, admin1) already scan at least 5000 parent rows, before target scans, ingestion or derived records. Under the literal repeated-scan charge it cannot complete. This is a bounded accounting counterexample, not an executed graph-runtime failure; an implementation operating on distinct native relations and expanding occurrences only once can avoid it, but that physical plan is not yet specified.

Repair: add an explicit ledger table covering input admission, unique provider/cache records, derived native records, occurrence expansion, DALgo scans, result replacement, retained provenance/status bytes, failures and continuation. Define which event spends the 5000 cumulative intermediate allowance and which spends processing/candidate or live-retention allowance. Do not silently raise a cap or exempt fan-out. Supply the actual finite local relation plan and a worked budget receipt for this 1000-parent case plus the accepted repeated-location/76-alias witness, with the same deadlines/output bounds. Reserve parent/incomplete-status capacity before child work. The plan should prevent both double charging of mere references and uncharged allocations.

## Scoped acceptance retained

- A new explicit contract capability is warranted: formats 1/2/3 cannot express integer conversion, a two-field composite or reverse many-side enumeration without changing their identity-only meaning. The one-level format 4 wrapper reuses the existing single attachment seam and preserves old bytes. Its exact numbering/wrapper design is reasonable, not a uniquely necessary architecture.
- Closed graph IDs/topology/operator switches, full immutable source qualifications, independent canonical admission, unchanged user entry authority and no generic evaluator/registry are appropriate. The example intentionally remains inadmissible because publication pins are placeholders.
- Independently checked all six example grains against the exact models and all five edge fields/types. Organizations/string; locations/(entity-reference resolving to required string organization key, int ordinal); places/string; countries/string; admin1/string; aliases/string. P1 is int→string and P2 is ordered string/string→string. No model rewrite is required.
- Fail-closed old-reader behavior follows the actual closed format dispatch: OVDB Parse falls to schema1, Directory rejects unknown format, and app routes to schema1. Required executable zero-data/no-salvage regression remains an implementation gate, not a test claimed here.
- Source versus later attachment revisions, selected publisher manifest association, unique collection mapping, full four runtime pins, and native/serving key separation are adequate architectural requirements. Preparation proofs must remain independently admitted evidence.
- Per-edge eligible-key-set completeness, partial singleton conservatism, changed-parent invalidation, unchanged sibling coverage, deadline-preserving explicit continuation, historical-result separation and retained parents are coherent with the accepted runtime boundary.
- Three related result grains avoid alias Cartesian expansion. Source metadata/source-data proof remain distinct; graph discovery must never load SQLite/chunks/user data. Legacy label-bridge metadata dependencies must be explicitly included in M1's closure accounting.

The current publisher default-activation repair and app PR195 remain separately landable on their own reviews. This review introduces no dependency requiring them to implement the graph. The supplied `65ebc741…` object was inspected for the current metadata bound; no new allegation about its two repaired transport budget findings is made here. This review approves no execution, source promotion, deployment or whole-wave completion.

## Re-review gate

Return a revised MD/JSON/example packet with M1 restored/measured, M2's concrete pre-debit mechanism and M3's ledger/finite physical plan plus ordinary-capacity receipts. Existing source/semantic pins and the independently accepted P1/P2/P3 decision stay unchanged.

VERDICT: blockers=0 majors=3 minors=0 land=no

# Native graph architecture independent review r2

**Scoped verdict: accept the revised architecture for root consideration and bounded implementation. M1, M2 and M3 are resolved; no remaining architecture findings.** This accepts neither executable publication nor a production runtime. Reviewer: fresh independent Codex reviewer continuing the same review lane, local macOS, 2026-10-05. Root remains sole lander. No semantic reconciliation was reopened and no repository, service or source data changed.

Reviewed proposal MD `e22e32ddb94779982cf26fe9fb9bfbb9ba125f29cdaa6f86029bfaec96b08775`, proposal JSON `8e8b9ebd7f392d1e18baa796ecb3f4e7e1d9ab8a3cbbe48246f2c66983e296ff`, packet JSON `11eb52eb3968720356fdaeea80ca20d8717fa79195d05f41173e4e7c2203fab4`. Independently verified all eleven packet file hashes/lengths and preserved r1 hashes. Claims below concern exact objects and private probes, not live heads, CI, deployment or browser acceptance.

## Findings disposition

**M1 resolved.** The one metadata operation now retains the accepted 2,097,152-byte aggregate, 96-reference and reference-depth-8 limits. I independently read all 42 known closure Git objects and verified immutable tuples, byte lengths and hashes, plus all three concrete provisional files: 445,186 known + 71,185 provisional = **516,371 bytes / 45 references**, leaving **1,580,781 bytes / 51 references**. The closure is explicitly incomplete and the listed final-publication holes are real gates. The three baseline indexes are concrete sizing inputs, not proof they admit this graph. Any discover-all reads must share the allowance or belong to a separate explicit operation as stated. Reference-depth annotations are a proposed traversal bound, not an executed production resolver trace; final resolver instrumentation must confirm depth. No cap increase remains.

**M2 resolved.** The new contract fixes each invocation to two leaf relations, one left cross-side string equality and an explicit hash algorithm, with no alternative shape or streaming path. Inspection of exact DALgo `1534acd4…` confirms the leaf/cross-side conditions make hash available; the selected hint chooses it; and the evaluator charges the size of the matching bucket. Thus `C = sum h(left.key)` and `Rout = C + unmatched-left-count` are exact for this closed shape. `maxResultRows=max(L,R,Rout,1)` also covers DALgo's leaf-array checks. A C=0 call can safely pass a per-call floor of 1 while charging zero pairs: no eligible bucket pairs exist. App-owned predebits, immutable input generations and no post-start refunds remove reliance on private counters. Repeated calls spend again; reference reuse makes no new call.

My independent exact-source DALgo probe exercised 60 finite cases including duplicate many-side keys, unmatched keys, empty targets and zero inputs. All output formulas matched; all 44 cases with C>1 refused C−1 and passed C. A separately owned reservation harness retained debits after an injected cache failure and charged recomputation again. These prove the architecture formula and API seam, not the future app guard implementation.

**M3 resolved.** The event table and native-level physical plan now distinguish newly materialized records from repeated pointer scans. Inputs, provider records, P1/P2 records, every reserved engine output, and each affiliation/location/alias occurrence are charged. Allocated copies stored as another relation remain chargeable; typed views and pointer indexes retain byte accounting. Failures and replacement allocations do not refund cumulative rows. Running the downstream joins on distinct native relations avoids five repeated affiliation-sized materializations. Parent/result/status holds prevent child work from consuming the space needed to retain parents.

I rehashed both native SQLite files and checked every supplied native witness row through immutable read-only SQLite: five ordinary-case rows and 46 multiplicity-case rows. Independent row-count calculations reproduce:

| Case | Cumulative intermediate | Candidates | Retained outputs |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| 1000 affiliations, one organization/location, aliases off | 3011 | 1004 | 2000 |
| Two affiliations, two native locations, 38 native aliases | 180 | 48 | 82 |

The second case has four location occurrences and 76 alias occurrences. These controls leave the accepted eight-row semantic fixture untouched. The byte receipts remain architecture witness serialization: the claimed two-copy arithmetic is correct, but actual app transport, indexes, intermediate token pairs, metadata/provenance and simultaneous buffers must all be reserved and measured in implementation. The proposal explicitly requires this and does not claim a 5 MiB JavaScript heap bound.

## Remaining gates, without architecture scope expansion

1. Freeze the committed semantic decision, graph wrapper, all final canonical indexes and outer-provider dependency tuples, graph admission/mapping evidence, publisher manifests, generated runtime manifests and required public descriptor/licence/route evidence. Rewalk and hash the actual full closure with the one shared metadata reader; preserve 2 MiB/96/depth8 and zero data queries during discovery. Spare baseline capacity grants no authority.
2. Implement and independently test the closed graph/schema, old-reader whole-wrapper refusal, no legacy salvage, source/model/entity-key/manifest association, full plan identity and four runtime pins. Keep the accepted P1/P2/P3 semantics and native snapshots unchanged.
3. Make the production reservation system atomic before allocation and execution, including fixed status holds, engine retention, actual typed serialization and transfer/staging buffers. Prove closed-shape rejection, immutable arrays, no refund after start, all related-set row bounds, failure and recomputation charging, and abort/deadline behavior. Architecture scripts are not production budget guards.
4. Exercise ordinary runtime reads and the actual Worker/service/storage/browser path: explicit actions only; same-run deadline on continuation; changed eligible-key-set invalidation; sibling independence; old results kept historical; all parents/statuses retained; exact native-to-serving collection guards; measured cancellation through the driver. Complete independent J1–J6 and canonical publication/admission gates before enabling execution.

The separate publisher activation, app PR195 and new runtime implementation lanes acquire no graph dependency from this approval; each retains its own verification and delivery gates. No CI verdict is asserted here.

Evidence: `checks-r2.json`, `check-r2.py`, `dalgo-checks-r2.json`, `probe-r2.mjs`; the r1 exact-source extraction remains the pinned DALgo execution input. No live network or publication was performed.

VERDICT: blockers=0 majors=0 minors=0 land=yes
