# ECB FX readiness research input — 5 October 2026

Read-only repository basis: `datatug/datatug origin/main@424c39a9d8fae2e4c5506b76033e70783239b86c`; read via `git show`, matched by live `git ls-remote`. Full programme brief read. Existing d1 candidate/source/dataset/evidence/assertions and W3 catalogue/P1 follow-up read. Research input needs independent review before governed incorporation. Nothing was implemented, reconciled, selected, deployed or published.

## Measured upstream bytes

Four official HTTPS downloads fetched without redirects, maximum 16 MiB per response. `probe.json` contains timestamps, hashes, HTTP metadata and all 41 per-currency bounds. `format-coverage-check.json` preserves bounded format checks. These raw files are temporary evidence only.

| Download | Bytes | Observed scope |
|---|---:|---|
| Full historical XML | 8,191,474 | 7,106 dates, 221,122 observations, 41 currency codes; 1999-01-04 to 2026-10-02 |
| Full historical CSV ZIP | 640,414 | One CSV member, 1,924,664 bytes; same 7,106 dates and 221,122 nonmissing decimal observations as XML |
| Last-90-days XML | 70,584 | 65 publication dates, 1,885 observations; 2026-07-06 to 2026-10-02 |
| Latest XML | 1,547 | 2026-10-02; 29 quoted currencies |

CSV is wide Date/currency columns, decimal-dot strings, N/A for unavailable values, trailing empty column. XML nests time-bearing Cube elements with currency/rate children. Preserve namespaces, dates and raw decimal rates; do not convert missing to zero. Bounds describe downloaded quotes, not currency validity. EUR is an explicit base and has no native quote row. DEM, FRF and VEB are absent from the entire historical download. RUB ends 2022-03-01; HRK 2022-12-30; BGN 2025-12-31. ROL/RON and TRL/TRY are distinct source codes, never aliases inferred by trimming or substituting. ISK has 4,765 observations across the overall range, so a min/max range does not imply continuous coverage. Weekend 2026-10-03/04 are absent. Observation at 10:25 UTC on Monday 5 October precedes normal afternoon publication: absence of a 5 October row is not evidence of a failed refresh.

## Official conditions refreshed

[ECB rates page](https://www.ecb.europa.eu/stats/policy_and_exchange_rates/euro_reference_exchange_rates/html/index.en.html): selected currencies quoted against EUR; usually updated around 16:00 CET on working days except TARGET closures; informational rates, discouraged for transaction use; suspended RUB publication since 1 March 2022. Historical CSV ZIP, XML, 90-day XML and SDMX formats are offered.

[ECB copyright conditions](https://www.ecb.europa.eu/services/using-our-site/disclaimer/html/index.en.html): free reuse has custom conditions: accurately reproduce and cite ECB; explicitly identify modifications; where incorporated in sold documents, tell buyers before fees and each time accessed that ECB supplies the information free. Business/promotional links must open the full browser window. Author-named documents have a separate permission exception. Retain ECB custom terms; do not invent CC0/CC-BY/SPDX licensing. These observations support a conditional attributed snapshot proposal, but do not constitute product-specific legal acceptance. Confirm how paid DataTug access meets the notice condition, and retain terms provenance with the release.

[Framework, 23 June 2026](https://www.ecb.europa.eu/stats/pdf/exchange/Frameworkfortheeuroforeignexchangereferencerates.en.pdf): reference rates are intended for information and not for direct/indirect market transaction benchmarks; currency coverage may change. It does not make historical reference data real-time trade prices.

## Proposed serving and refresh shape — unimplemented

One ordinary OVDB recordset, source-faithful normalized rows keyed by publication date + quote currency, explicit EUR base, decimal rate, provider/rate-kind metadata and snapshot provenance. Preserve original decimals and absence. Index exact date/currency; do not materialize every currency-pair combination. Existing manifest/source mechanisms and HTTPS controls should be reused after the serving capability gate passes.

A full pinned history is economical: compressed CSV is under 1 MiB and full XML under 8 MiB. Proposed download cap 16 MiB, unpack cap 8 MiB, 256 MiB RSS, 2 minutes per refresh; these are budgets to measure, not validated runtime performance. Use full CSV initially with XML parity as independent source-format evidence; version parser and hash input/output. After publication, bounded daily or 90-day window refresh plus periodic full rebuild can detect historical corrections; daily-only append cannot prove historical integrity. Start with reviewed full-history refresh if simpler. No scheduler, paid service, daemon or new provider repository is authorized here. Fetch time, HTTP Last-Modified, latest publication date and snapshot/hash are separate fields; last-good data must remain labeled if refresh fails.

First practical journey: user explicitly declares currency and date, chooses indicative same-date lookup, sees supported/unmatched dates/codes and source information. A EUR-base lookup can demonstrate useful rates before arbitrary pair comparisons are reconciled. This is a proposal, not an accepted new user contract or a launch claim.

## Separate fresh reconciliation remains required

`d1-mapping-ecb-rate` already accepts the narrow source-scoped EUR quote; preserve that disposition. `d1-edge-aw-fx-currentref` and `d1-edge-ecb-currency-validity` remain unresolved. Scope the fresh work to existing 14 AW target currencies, one supported same-day pair, one missing date and DEM/FRF/VEB negatives. Decide date-only versus instant/day policy, source publication versus fixture rate date, AverageRate/EndOfDayRate versus indicative reference kind, directed pair, decimal precision and whether an EUR identity leg is permitted as a labeled derivation. Two non-EUR legs must share the exact publication date: quote-per-EUR/base-per-EUR is the proposed quote-per-base calculation, not native ECB transaction data. Missing dates stay unavailable unless an explicit separately reviewed carry policy is chosen; never silently use latest/previous day. Preserve null/zero/obsolete code negatives.

Currency/date does not identify a territory: CLDR regional assignment intervals can multiply rates. Scope any currency-only projection or region/tender selection explicitly. Do not infer currencies from customer country, salary amount or bare monetary columns. No cross-currency total without an accepted amount/currency/time contract.

## Priority delta and later exact record updates

User: “Would be good to have something like currency exchange rates”. ECB remains existing W3 conditional candidate. Proposed delta: prioritize bounded FX reconciliation/readiness immediately after the current W1 gate, then let root decide a small reference-lookup packet versus the broader existing W2/W3 order. Preserve all candidates, W1 scope, B1, F1–F6, source rights and actual browser acceptance. No automatic expansion, lifecycle promotion or wave renumbering.

`priority-delta-proposal.json` lists exact existing evidence/candidate/portfolio paths for later governed incorporation. Reconciler decisions must update their assertion records through the existing mechanism; this researcher makes no semantic decision. Current main orchestration retains all landing/publication ownership and independent-review authority.

ROL/RON and TRL/TRY are distinct source codes, never aliases inferred by trimming or substituting. ISK has 4,765 observations across the overall range, so a min/max range does not imply continuous coverage. Weekend 2026-10-03/04 are absent. Observation at 10:25 UTC on Monday 5 October precedes normal afternoon publication: absence of a 5 October row is not evidence of a failed refresh.

Raw-format fidelity observation from independent r1 review: latest daily XML and full history agree numerically, but six daily/history rate strings differ only in trailing zeros: CZK 24.470/24.47, SEK 11.2900/11.29, ISK 137.00/137, TRY 55.1650/55.165, BRL 5.8610/5.861 and THB 37.710/37.71. Retain each source format and original raw string; future parity checks must distinguish numeric agreement from lexical fidelity. Historical CSV/XML raw strings match. This note makes no precision, rounding or cross-rate semantic decision.

## Official conditions refreshed

[ECB rates page](https://www.ecb.europa.eu/stats/policy_and_exchange_rates/euro_reference_exchange_rates/html/index.en.html): selected currencies quoted against EUR; usually updated around 16:00 CET on working days except TARGET closures; informational rates, discouraged for transaction use; suspended RUB publication since 1 March 2022. Historical CSV ZIP, XML, 90-day XML and SDMX formats are offered.

[ECB copyright conditions](https://www.ecb.europa.eu/services/using-our-site/disclaimer/html/index.en.html): free reuse has custom conditions: accurately reproduce and cite ECB; explicitly identify modifications; where incorporated in sold documents, tell buyers before fees and each time accessed that ECB supplies the information free. Business/promotional links must open the full browser window. Author-named documents have a separate permission exception. Retain ECB custom terms; do not invent CC0/CC-BY/SPDX licensing. These observations support a conditional attributed snapshot proposal, but do not constitute product-specific legal acceptance. Confirm how paid DataTug access meets the notice condition, and retain terms provenance with the release.

[Framework, 23 June 2026](https://www.ecb.europa.eu/stats/pdf/exchange/Frameworkfortheeuroforeignexchangereferencerates.en.pdf): reference rates are intended for information and not for direct/indirect market transaction benchmarks; currency coverage may change. It does not make historical reference data real-time trade prices.

**Canonical custom-terms representation is an open publication gate.** Independent review verified `openvaultdb/ovdb origin/main@1a2d90171ab4a7ab5ac02baa95b36192e07fe919`; this repair also read the exact pinned `internal/publisher/manifest/publisher.go`. Lines 16–20 accept only 18 enumerated SPDX licence IDs; lines 32–38 permit only model/meaning/data licence keys and no terms-reference field; lines 108–115 reject licence values outside the enumeration. Neither the research label `ECB reuse conditions` nor an ECB `LicenseRef` is an accepted manifest value. Free-form research provenance and an adjacent README do not establish canonical publishability.

Before any selected/publishable/live claim, establish a reviewed existing compliant canonical mechanism, or obtain separate approval for a narrow extension, that faithfully represents ECB custom **source-data** terms and their URL/version or dated provenance, attribution, modification disclosure and applicable sold-document pre-payment/per-access free-availability notices. Demonstrate the actual artifact passes the applicable canonical publisher validators and registry/Directory acceptance checks, and retains the terms through discovery and serving. Do not substitute a fabricated SPDX identifier, relabel ECB data as CC0/CC-BY, conflate source-data rights with independently licensed model/meaning metadata, omit custom obligations or bypass validation. No existing compliant path is asserted in this packet; choosing or implementing one remains later governed work. This gate preserves ECB as a conditional candidate while blocking publication readiness claims.

## Proposed serving and refresh shape — unimplemented

One ordinary OVDB recordset, source-faithful normalized rows keyed by publication date + quote currency, explicit EUR base, decimal rate, provider/rate-kind metadata and snapshot provenance. Preserve original decimals and absence. Index exact date/currency; do not materialize every currency-pair combination. Reuse existing source/HTTPS mechanisms only after the serving capability gate and the explicit canonical custom-terms representation/validator/registry gate above pass. The current publisher limitation prevents assuming that an otherwise useful OVDB recordset can already be published.

A full pinned history is economical: compressed CSV is under 1 MiB and full XML under 8 MiB. Proposed download cap 16 MiB, unpack cap 8 MiB, 256 MiB RSS, 2 minutes per refresh; these are budgets to measure, not validated runtime performance. Use full CSV initially with XML parity as independent source-format evidence; version parser and hash input/output. After publication, bounded daily or 90-day window refresh plus periodic full rebuild can detect historical corrections; daily-only append cannot prove historical integrity. Start with reviewed full-history refresh if simpler. No scheduler, paid service, daemon or new provider repository is authorized here. Fetch time, HTTP Last-Modified, latest publication date and snapshot/hash are separate fields; last-good data must remain labeled if refresh fails.

First practical journey: user explicitly declares currency and date, chooses indicative same-date lookup, sees supported/unmatched dates/codes and source information. A EUR-base lookup can demonstrate useful rates before arbitrary pair comparisons are reconciled. This is a proposal, not an accepted new user contract or a launch claim.

`d1-mapping-ecb-rate` already accepts the narrow source-scoped EUR quote; preserve that disposition. `d1-edge-aw-fx-currentref` and `d1-edge-ecb-currency-validity` remain unresolved. Two non-EUR legs must share the exact publication date: quote-per-EUR/base-per-EUR is the proposed quote-per-base calculation, not native ECB transaction data. Missing dates stay unavailable unless an explicit separately reviewed carry policy is chosen; never silently use latest/previous day. Preserve null/zero/obsolete code negatives.

Currency/date does not identify a territory: CLDR regional assignment intervals can multiply rates. Scope any currency-only projection or region/tender selection explicitly. # Independent ECB FX readiness review — r1

Reviewer: `fx_readiness_review`, independent local Codex/macOS, distinct from the original researcher. Scope: source facts, frozen bytes and bounded priority readiness. No final semantic reconciliation, repository mutation, provider creation, publication, services or external messages.

## Scoped verdict

The ECB source facts and frozen counts are verified. The bounded FX follow-up can be prioritized after the current W1 gate while preserving the existing portfolio. One major documentation finding remains: the proposed serving gate must explicitly retain the present canonical custom-terms representation limitation. This review grants no selected, executable, live or blanket legal approval.

## Finding FX-R1-1 — major — open

`artifact:data-fabric-fx-priority-readiness/readiness.md:28` proposes reusing existing manifest mechanisms after the serving capability gate. `priority-delta-proposal.json` retains a generic licence/provenance gate. Neither names a concrete present limitation: the canonical OVDB publisher cannot represent ECB custom data terms through its accepted manifest licence values.

Independently verified `openvaultdb/ovdb origin/main@1a2d90171ab4a7ab5ac02baa95b36192e07fe919`, using `git ls-remote`. At that exact commit, `internal/publisher/manifest/publisher.go:16-20` enumerates 18 SPDX licence IDs; lines 32-38 permit only model/meaning/data within licences and no terms-reference field; lines 108-115 reject values outside that list. Neither `ECB reuse conditions` nor an ECB `LicenseRef` is accepted. The free-form research records do not establish canonical publishability.

Required fix: explicitly name canonical faithful custom-terms/provenance representation and validator/registry acceptance as a publication prerequisite. Require a reviewed existing compliant path or separately approved schema work. Preserve ECB attribution, modification disclosure, terms provenance and sold-document free-availability notices as applicable. Do not invent a standard SPDX licence, conflate data rights with metadata/model licences, or bypass validation. This blocks any publishable/selected/live claim; it does not reject ECB as a useful conditional research candidate. Fix or explicitly decline it before incorporating the readiness proposal as reviewed.

## Independent evidence

`datatug/datatug origin/main@424c39a9d8fae2e4c5506b76033e70783239b86c` independently matched `git ls-remote`. All exact paths proposed for later evidence/candidate/portfolio/assertion updates exist at that head. Their hashes, and hashes of the four reviewed research inputs, are in `review-r1.json`.

All four frozen downloads independently match the probe's SHA256 and byte length. XML parsing independently reproduces all date counts, observation counts, 41 per-currency historical bounds, namespaces and absence of duplicate date/quote keys. Full-history XML has 7,106 dates, 221,122 observations and 41 codes, 1999-01-04 through 2026-10-02. The ZIP contains one 1,924,664-byte CSV with the same 7,106 rows and 221,122 populated quote keys; every raw rate string matches historical XML. There are 70,224 N/A cells, plus the structurally empty trailing column. The 90-day XML has 65 dates and 1,885 quotes, and is an exact raw-value subset of history. Daily XML has one date and 29 quotes.

Additional observation, not a source defect: the latest daily XML and historical XML agree numerically, but six strings differ by trailing zeros: CZK 24.470/24.47, SEK 11.2900/11.29, ISK 137.00/137, TRY 55.1650/55.165, BRL 5.8610/5.861, THB 37.710/37.71 (daily/history). Preserve the original input format and raw values; future format-parity checks should distinguish numeric value from textual precision. This review makes no cross-rate rounding decision.

Original HTTP status, redirect count, header and observation timestamps are retained as the original request's recorded metadata, rather than reconstructed from frozen bytes. The official page separately supports the endpoint roles and observed 2 October date/USD quote. No repeated full 8 MiB source download was needed.

`independent-byte-checks.json` contains reproducible measured results. Frozen bytes contain no EUR quote row and no DEM/FRF/VEB observations. RUB ends 2022-03-01, HRK 2022-12-30 and BGN 2025-12-31. ROL/RON and TRL/TRY remain separate codes. ISK's 4,765 observations do not imply continuous coverage. Weekend 3/4 October and 5 October are absent in the recorded morning snapshot; the 10:25 UTC observation precedes normal afternoon publication. No false stale-refresh conclusion follows. Presence/bounds describe reference quotations, not legal-tender intervals or currency identity.

## Primary-source checks

[ECB rates page](https://www.ecb.europa.eu/stats/policy_and_exchange_rates/euro_reference_exchange_rates/html/index.en.html) independently supports EUR base, working-day updates around 16:00 CET except TARGET closures, information-only rates, discouraged transaction use, suspended RUB publication after its last rate on 1 March 2022, and CSV ZIP/XML/90-day/SDMX downloads. The reviewed web view also showed 2 October 2026 and USD 1.1225.

[ECB copyright conditions](https://www.ecb.europa.eu/services/using-our-site/disclaimer/html/index.en.html) support conditional reuse: reproduce accurately, credit ECB, label modifications; when incorporated in sold documents, disclose free availability before payment and on each access; business/promotional links must load the whole browser window. Author-named documents have a separate permission exception. These are custom terms, not inferred CC0/CC-BY or product-specific legal acceptance. Paid DataTug applicability and presentation must be resolved separately.

[ECB framework dated 23 June 2026](https://www.ecb.europa.eu/stats/pdf/exchange/Frameworkfortheeuroforeignexchangereferencerates.en.pdf) supports informational reference use, excludes intended market-transaction benchmark use, and allows coverage changes. It does not establish a trade-price or real-time service contract.

## Priority and reconciliation boundaries

At the pinned hub head, ECB is already a conditional W3 recordset and its two unresolved FX edges are already a priority-1 bounded follow-up. The proposed change is an ordering preference for fresh readiness/reconciliation and a later root decision on a small packet. It neither automatically moves W3 membership nor grants full international-catalogue completion.

Keep W1's exact five recordsets: country, places, admin1, alternates and ROR organizations. Preserve W2-W7 and every earlier candidate, dependency and gate. The portfolio records 682 original candidates, 1,170 original assertions, 57 original scenario/bundle rows and 37 proposed public recordsets; implemented recordsets and launch-ready scenarios remain zero at this snapshot. Preserve B1, F1-F6, source rights, accepted query semantics, canonical validation, independent exact-head review and a real browser journey. Resource figures are proposals to measure, not a performance receipt.

The existing `d1-mapping-ecb-rate` is reconciled and accepts only the source-scoped indicative EUR quote with provider/rate-kind/publication-date fidelity. Both `d1-edge-aw-fx-currentref` and `d1-edge-ecb-currency-validity` remain needs-review/unresolved. Their fresh decisions belong to a separate later reconciler. Preserve the 14 AW targets, supported same-date case, missing-day case, obsolete-code and null/zero negatives; no previous/latest fallback, currency inferred from country, or currency/date-to-territory uniqueness. Keep source quote kind distinct from AW AverageRate/EndOfDayRate. Arithmetic discussion here changes no assertion disposition.

# Independent app candidate review r1

**Component verdict: changes required; 0 blockers, 2 majors, 0 minors. Do not land candidate r1.** The findings concern bounded transport itself and can be repaired without changing semantic admission. Full Task 5 and production acceptance remain pending independently.

Reviewed locally with Codex on Alex macOS. Root owns landing. No author source files, commits, branches, remote refs, services, ports, browser state, publication or fixture bytes were changed.

## Frozen scope and evidence

Candidate: `artifact:data-fabric-w1-app-bounded-runtime/candidate-r1.json`; base/HEAD `413bb772e04f139210adec92ad0cb3fce2b07883`; exact 20-file patch SHA256 `cae2c0ab10c94a24f356cd8c1502c86982b6e89b24e5114ef0a69f97048a0e3a`.

Independently hashed all 20 frozen file bytes and all 23 native fixture files. Every candidate hash matches; native fixture bytes also match `git show` at the stated base. Rechecked after testing. Author log hashes match their manifest, which proves log identity, not independent execution. See `verification-r1.json`.

Read accepted runtime adapter architecture r3, native table serving boundary r2, app semantic-execution-gap r1, repository AGENTS and the relevant Nx/UI/WB instructions. Native diagnostic-table selection belongs to publisher/runtime admission and has not been silently replaced by an app allowlist.

## Findings

### M1 — [P2] Refuse network dispatch at zero remaining decoded bytes

`libs/datatug/main/src/lib/queries/public-data/immutable-federation.ts:247-248,288-306,327-331`; related `bounded-run-budget.ts:33-58`.

The pre-request `budget.check()` checks only cancellation/deadline. `consumeNetwork()` aborts only above the cap, so reaching it exactly leaves the run dispatchable. The next HTTP request starts before `budget.remaining` reaches the streaming guard. A synthetic driver response exactly equal to the configured byte budget followed by its dependent read produced **2 HTTP calls instead of 1**. The second body then failed its bound.

This is a pre-dispatch contract failure, not a claim that oversized rows were returned successfully. The accepted architecture states that no new request starts when a counter is exhausted. An ordinary success needs a nonempty JSON envelope; probing for a zero-body response is neither necessary nor authorized by that contract. Add a separate network-admission guard before every actual fetch, including driver/continuation reads, without rejecting a response that legitimately completes exactly at the cap or forbidding local result reads.

### M2 — [P2] Honor lower configured place-identifier bounds

`libs/datatug/main/src/lib/queries/public-data/immutable-federation.ts:222-230`; related `bounded-federation.ts:73-82` and `federated-query-executor.ts:234`.

The new branch uses `bounds.identifierLimit` only for the first ROR lookup and hard-codes 100 for every other lookup. A valid place configuration with `identifierLimit: 1` and two distinct selected keys (`USA`, `Canada`) sends both keys and succeeds. The prior bounded transport compares against `bounds.identifierLimit`; validation still accepts values 1–100 and the result policy still advertises the supplied smaller limit.

The absolute 100-key ceiling is intact. The defect is violation of a stricter reviewed/caller-selected bound. Apply that declared bound to the initial place lookup while preserving the appropriate absolute caps for later stages; test both the exact chosen bound and one over it with no dependent request on refusal.

## Independent execution

Built a scratch workspace by extracting the exact base with `git archive` and copying the 20 hash-verified frozen files. Appended only the two regressions above to the scratch copy of `immutable-federation.spec.ts`. The original candidate files stayed unchanged. `independent-regressions.patch` preserves the added test cases.

Resolved `datatug-main` live through Nx: test `@nx/vitest:test`, lint `@nx/eslint:lint`, build `@nx/angular:ng-packagr-lite`, matching the supplied resolved-target receipt. Used the locally cached exact pnpm 11.26.0 entrypoint because generic pnpm 11.20.0 attempted a version switch. The first scratch invocation tried pnpm's automatic install and was refused by its unsafe-modules-directory guard before replacing the shared dependency directory. The recorded test invocation uses `pnpm_config_verify_deps_before_run=warn` solely to prevent dependency installation for the scratch copy. It emitted the expected workspace-structure warning. No dependencies were installed or changed.

Executed in `artifact:data-fabric-w1-app-independent/workspace`:

```text
NX_DAEMON=false NX_ISOLATE_PLUGINS=false pnpm_config_verify_deps_before_run=warn
wb run -- node private-reference:pnpm.mjs nx run datatug-main:test --watch=false --skip-nx-cache --testFiles=src/lib/queries/public-data/immutable-federation.spec.ts,src/lib/queries/federated-query.service.spec.ts,src/lib/queries/federated-query.worker.spec.ts,src/lib/chat/chat-null-parity.spec.ts
```

Result: **2 new regressions failed; 167 pre-existing candidate tests passed across 4 files**. This includes immutable transport 24 existing tests, service 5, worker 4 and SQLite parity 134. Full output and hashes: `tests-r1.log`, `verification-r1.json`. No full-suite, lint or build rerun is claimed. Installed shared dependencies were reused; this is not a clean-lockfile-install receipt.

The SQLite test change is exactly one `@vitest-environment node` directive. Its real `node:sqlite` database/assertions are retained and all 134 tests ran successfully; no skip, replacement engine or assertion removal was introduced.

Temporary node_modules symlinks in both the author worktree and scratch copy were removed. The canonical dependency directory is preserved.

## Scoped positive assessment and remaining gates

- All four pin response checks reject changed/missing values before rows are accepted. Initial per-database requests are serialized, subsequent collections/continuations use the captured full identity, and a failed network page aborts the shared run rather than serving that page from stale success.
- Ordinary requests are explicit POST/no-store, redirect-refusing, with at most 1000 rows and no snapshot paging headers. DALgo pages accepted local data; full source pages stay possibly-more. Continuation shares the original budget/deadline and cumulative receipts; skipped offsets and changed parent filters do not establish completeness.
- Separate materialized-output accounting, intermediate/final row limits, absolute key limits, and partial/unresolved diagnostic treatment are present. The two findings qualify budget admission and configured place limits.
- Service cancellation/deadline invokes Worker.terminate and owns the two exact temporary database names; worker/component harnesses are synthetic. These tests support component behavior, not real browser Worker shutdown, in-flight server cancellation, Cloud/CORS or mounted driver release. Those remain later acceptance gates as requested.
- Explicit saves bind observed full pins to the executed plan. Production discovery/saved public-data execution remains unconditionally closed; arbitrary runtime configuration supplies no canonical admission. Construction/reopening does not initiate the new transport. Historical local result paging after deadline is intentionally distinct from further source execution.
- The recorded integer/string, composite admin1 and full location graph semantic gap remains unresolved and assigned to the specialist. This review neither invents coercions nor presents the generic configured transport as full Task 5 readiness. Published Directory/runtime metadata, admitted source semantics, live browser no-action/continuation/cancellation journeys and full runtime acceptance remain pending even after these two fixes.

VERDICT: blockers=0 majors=2 minors=0 land=no

**Component verdict: approve additive bounded-transport preparation landing.** Both r1 majors are resolved; no new actionable finding in the three-file repair delta. Root remains sole landing owner. This verdict does not complete Task 5 or authorize runtime/Directory publication or wider semantic execution.

## Exact scope

Local Codex review on Alex macOS. Read handoff-r2, candidate-r2 and the full repair delta against the retained r1 review. Base/HEAD remains `413bb772e04f139210adec92ad0cb3fce2b07883`.

The other 17 files retain their r1 hashes. Final recheck passed after testing. ## Findings resolved

**M1 resolved.** `bounded-run-budget.ts:52-58` introduces distinct network admission at `>= maximumBytes`. `immutable-federation.ts:161,293` calls it before both actual fetch sites. The narrow exception at lines413-416 leaves previously accepted local data readable after a network-admission refusal, while the streaming over-limit and ordinary failure abort behavior remains intact. Both original r1 counterexamples now pass. Independent additional tests establish a complete joined result whose cumulative responses equal the cap, refusal of another source page with no extra HTTP call, and continued access to the accepted local rows without an abort. A changed-manifest continuation still rejects, aborts, and prevents a later local cache read from returning stale success.

**M2 resolved.** `immutable-federation.ts:228-234` applies the configured identifier limit whenever the parent is the initial source, regardless of place/ROR kind. Later native stages retain the absolute100 ceiling. Original lower-place-limit refusal and exact-limit/deduplication tests pass. Additional independent tests verify a lower initial ROR limit of1 refuses two valid ROR URLs before target fetch, and an initial ROR limit of1 does not wrongly reduce subsequent native-place capacity:100 succeeds,101 refuses before the later request.

No findings declined or deferred within this narrow repair scope.

## Independent execution and receipts

Created `artifact:data-fabric-w1-app-independent/workspace-r2` from the exact base via `git archive`, then copied all20 hash-verified candidate files. Added five independent test cases only in that scratch copy. The candidate already contains the two original independent r1 regressions and the author's boundary tests.

```text
wb run -- node private-reference:pnpm.mjs nx run datatug-main:test --watch=false --skip-nx-cache --testFiles=src/lib/queries/public-data/immutable-federation.spec.ts
```

**38/38 tests passed, exit0:33 candidate cases plus5 independent additions.** Tests exercised installed DALgo, fake IndexedDB and synthetic fetch bodies; no actual network/browser runtime proof is claimed. Used the target resolved in r1, unchanged in this delta. Shared installed dependencies were reused unchanged; pnpm's warning mode prevents an automatic install for the scratch workspace. The scratch-only node_modules symlink was removed after execution. Author worktree dependencies remained absent; canonical dependencies were preserved.

Evidence: `tests-r2.log`, `independent-regressions-r2.patch`, `verification-r2.json` preserve output, added cases, exact argv/env, hashes and cleanup checks.

Independently matched all five supplied author receipt/log hashes and inspected final summaries. Their full target records162 files/2290 tests passing; lint records zero findings; the uncached production build and four dependency targets succeed. Exact argv/environment/timestamps are now recorded. These are inspected author executions, not additional independent full-suite/lint/build runs. The unchanged real Node SQLite assertions were independently exercised in r1 (134 passed); the r2 delta does not change that file.

## Approval boundary

Approve the component candidate for additive preparation landing on the reviewed base, subject to root's ordinary landing checks. Production discovery and saved-publicData execution closure, pin validation, worker lifecycle and UI/save paths retain their r1-reviewed bytes. Real browser Worker/server cancellation, no-action and continuation journeys, final admitted Directory/runtime metadata, semantic contract binding/branching/completeness, and wider J1–J6/Task5 acceptance remain separate gates. No semantic coercion or full-journey readiness is inferred from these repairs.
